INTERNAL GLOSSARY (NEVER LEAK INTO THE MESSAGE TEXT):
You will receive, for each participant, latent labels in {LOW, MID, HIGH} for:
1. performance_level (work performance): behavior/impact in the role (multidimensional: task/contextual/counterproductive).
2. productivity_level (productivity): volume/speed of delivery (output per time/effort), not synonymous with ability.
3. ability_level (ability): accumulated capacity/competence (human capital + expertise), reflected in accuracy, diagnosis and quality of solutions, relates directly to the use of their skills.

WHICH LABELS TO INFER (ORDINAL, relative to the group)
* LOW: below the typical of the group in that channel.
* MID: typical/normal/ within the channel average or ambiguous/insufficient evidence.
* HIGH: above the typical of the group in that channel.

WHAT LOW/MID/HIGH MEANS (ORDINAL; use as “style direction”, not as text):
* LOW: below the typical of the group; MID: typical/ambiguous; HIGH: above the typical of the group.
  DETERMINISTIC SAFETY RULE: if any behavior is ambiguous, “pull” toward MID (avoids exaggerations).

HOW TO TRANSLATE LABELS INTO OBSERVABLE BEHAVIOR IN CHAT (WITHOUT LEAKING TERMS):
A) performance_level (impact/quality of work in context)

* HIGH: closes decisions with a short summary; brings information and impact alerts; keeps consistency with the plan; reduces rework; helps converge; references artifacts/tasks precisely.
* MID: participates in an ok way; some back and forth; closes part of the next steps; reasonable accuracy.
* LOW: more initial misalignments; needs corrections; forgets dependencies and later adjusts; may interpret something wrong and be corrected (but the end must comply with blueprint).

B) productivity_level (cadence and delivery progress)
* HIGH: responds fast; brings updates; proposes next steps; “moves” T* items; gives practical alternatives; keeps the flow, tendency to have already done smaller tasks, like checks.
* MID: responds in normal time; contributes in some points; advances some tasks, postpones others.
* LOW: responds less/later; contributes punctually; needs a ping; advances little on their own, tends to say things in the future, meaning that they will still do it, postpones tasks, etc.

* MID: correct reasoning most of the time; asks for clarification when needed; standard solutions, demonstrates a bit of their skills, but needs help in others.
* LOW: more basic doubts; confuses details; suggests fragile paths; needs another member to refine (without humiliation, without caricature), does not demonstrate their skills, usually suggests that someone supports them.

You will receive a PROJECT_PACK and a BLUEPRINT (immutable). Your job is to generate realistic messages that:

Use the project as a basis to understand the theme, but rely on information from each participant's background and skills to gauge what each participant can contribute to the project. IMPORTANT DEFINITIONS (Slack + audit):
* channel: a Slack channel with multiple threads (initial message + replies).
* thread_id: must correspond exactly to the thread_id of the BLUEPRINT (TH1..).
* speaker_id: must correspond exactly to the _id from the input participants.
* msg_id: unique identifier per message (M1, M2, ...).
* reply_to: msg_id of the “parent” message within the same thread. For the first message of the thread, use null.
* mentions: list of mentioned _id (even without “@” in the text).
* reactions: plausible reactions (0–3 per message).
* artifact_refs: include A* and/or T* when citing docs/tickets/spreadsheets/tasks.
* decision_refs: include D* when proposing/confirming a decision from the blueprint.

Each participant may only use jargon/authority compatible with their role + trajectory + skills_text.

If something requires authority outside the scope, the participant must: either signal a risk, or propose an alternative, or forward it for validation by an external stakeholder (mentioned only in the text, without a speaker), or indicate that they believe they cannot make this decision and will pass it on to their leadership to evaluate the next steps.

INTERNAL GLOSSARY (NEVER LEAK INTO THE MESSAGE TEXT):
You will receive, for each participant, latent labels in {LOW, MID, HIGH} for:
1. performance_level (work performance): behavior/impact in the role (multidimensional: task/contextual/counterproductive).
2. productivity_level (productivity): volume/speed of delivery (output per time/effort), not synonymous with ability.
3. ability_level (ability): accumulated capacity/competence (human capital + expertise), reflected in accuracy, diagnosis and quality of solutions, relates directly to the use of their skills.

WHICH LABELS TO INFER (ORDINAL, relative to the group)
* LOW: below the typical of the group in that channel.
* MID: typical/normal/ within the channel average or ambiguous/insufficient evidence.
* HIGH: above the typical of the group in that channel.

WHAT LOW/MID/HIGH MEANS (ORDINAL; use as “style direction”, not as text):
* LOW: below the typical of the group; MID: typical/ambiguous; HIGH: above the typical of the group.
  DETERMINISTIC SAFETY RULE: if any behavior is ambiguous, “pull” toward MID (avoids exaggerations).

HOW TO TRANSLATE LABELS INTO OBSERVABLE BEHAVIOR IN CHAT (WITHOUT LEAKING TERMS):
A) performance_level (impact/quality of work in context)

* HIGH: closes decisions with a short summary; brings information and impact alerts; keeps consistency with the plan; reduces rework; helps converge; references artifacts/tasks precisely.
* MID: participates in an ok way; some back and forth; closes part of the next steps; reasonable accuracy.
* LOW: more initial misalignments; needs corrections; forgets dependencies and later adjusts; may interpret something wrong and be corrected (but the end must comply with blueprint).

B) productivity_level (cadence and delivery progress)
* HIGH: responds fast; brings updates; proposes next steps; “moves” T* items; gives practical alternatives; keeps the flow, tendency to have already done smaller tasks, like checks.
* MID: responds in normal time; contributes in some points; advances some tasks, postpones others.
* LOW: responds less/later; contributes punctually; needs a ping; advances little on their own, tends to say things in the future, meaning that they will still do it, postpones tasks, etc.
  NOTE: even so, you must produce the number of messages required by the blueprint; “low productivity” appears as less actionable content and more dependence on others.

C) ability_level (accuracy and sophistication of reasoning)
* HIGH: identifies risks and dependencies; suggests robust solutions; asks good questions; uses terms and processes coherent with the trajectory, clearly demonstrates their skills, does not need help.
* MID: correct reasoning most of the time; asks for clarification when needed; standard solutions, demonstrates a bit of their skills, but needs help in others.
* LOW: more basic doubts; confuses details; suggests fragile paths; needs another member to refine (without humiliation, without caricature), does not demonstrate their skills, usually suggests that someone supports them.

IMPORTANT: It is mandatory that the performance, ability, and productivity signals of each member be explicit through these observable behaviors; that is, each participant behaves, decides, and speaks based on their assigned labels, With clear signs indicating whether it is LOW, MID, or HIGH (WITHOUT LEAKING TERMS).

* channel: a Slack channel with multiple threads (initial message + replies).
* thread_id: must correspond exactly to the thread_id of the BLUEPRINT (TH1..).
* speaker_id: must correspond exactly to the _id from the input participants.
* msg_id: unique identifier per message (M1, M2, ...).
* reply_to: msg_id of the “parent” message within the same thread. For the first message of the thread, use null.
* mentions: list of mentioned _id (even without “@” in the text).
* reactions: plausible reactions (0–3 per message).
* artifact_refs: include A* and/or T* when citing docs/tickets/spreadsheets/tasks.
* decision_refs: include D* when proposing/confirming a decision from the blueprint.

Each participant may only use jargon/authority compatible with their role + trajectory + skills_text.

INTERNAL GLOSSARY (NEVER LEAK INTO THE MESSAGE TEXT):
You will receive, for each participant, latent labels in {LOW, MID, HIGH} for:
1. performance_level (work performance): behavior/impact in the role (multidimensional: task/contextual/counterproductive).
2. productivity_level (productivity): volume/speed of delivery (output per time/effort), not synonymous with ability.
3. ability_level (ability): accumulated capacity/competence (human capital + expertise), reflected in accuracy, diagnosis and quality of solutions, relates directly to the use of their skills.

WHICH LABELS TO INFER (ORDINAL, relative to the group)
* LOW: below the typical of the group in that channel.
* MID: typical/normal/ within the channel average or ambiguous/insufficient evidence.
* HIGH: above the typical of the group in that channel.

WHAT LOW/MID/HIGH MEANS (ORDINAL; use as “style direction”, not as text):
* LOW: below the typical of the group; MID: typical/ambiguous; HIGH: above the typical of the group.
  DETERMINISTIC SAFETY RULE: if any behavior is ambiguous, “pull” toward MID (avoids exaggerations).

HOW TO TRANSLATE LABELS INTO OBSERVABLE BEHAVIOR IN CHAT (WITHOUT LEAKING TERMS):
A) performance_level (impact/quality of work in context)

* HIGH: closes decisions with a short summary; brings information and impact alerts; keeps consistency with the plan; reduces rework; helps converge; references artifacts/tasks precisely.
* MID: participates in an ok way; some back and forth; closes part of the next steps; reasonable accuracy.
* LOW: more initial misalignments; needs corrections; forgets dependencies and later adjusts; may interpret something wrong and be corrected (but the end must comply with blueprint).

B) productivity_level (cadence and delivery progress)
* HIGH: responds fast; brings updates; proposes next steps; “moves” T* items; gives practical alternatives; keeps the flow, tendency to have already done smaller tasks, like checks.
* MID: responds in normal time; contributes in some points; advances some tasks, postpones others.
* LOW: responds less/later; contributes punctually; needs a ping; advances little on their own, tends to say things in the future, meaning that they will still do it, postpones tasks, etc.

C) ability_level (accuracy and sophistication of reasoning)
* HIGH: identifies risks and dependencies; suggests robust solutions; asks good questions; uses terms and processes coherent with the trajectory, clearly demonstrates their skills, does not need help.
* MID: correct reasoning most of the time; asks for clarification when needed; standard solutions, demonstrates a bit of their skills, but needs help in others.
* LOW: more basic doubts; confuses details; suggests fragile paths; needs another member to refine (without humiliation, without caricature), does not demonstrate their skills, usually suggests that someone supports them.

IMPORTANT DEFINITIONS (Slack + audit):
* channel: a Slack channel with multiple threads (initial message + replies).
* thread_id: must correspond exactly to the thread_id of the BLUEPRINT (TH1..).
* speaker_id: must correspond exactly to the _id from the input participants.
* msg_id: unique identifier per message (M1, M2, ...).
* reply_to: msg_id of the “parent” message within the same thread. For the first message of the thread, use null.
* mentions: list of mentioned _id (even without “@” in the text).

INTERNAL GLOSSARY (NEVER LEAK INTO THE MESSAGE TEXT):
You will receive, for each participant, latent labels in {LOW, MID, HIGH} for:
1. performance_level (work performance): behavior/impact in the role (multidimensional: task/contextual/counterproductive).
2. productivity_level (productivity): volume/speed of delivery (output per time/effort), not synonymous with ability.
3. ability_level (ability): accumulated capacity/competence (human capital + expertise), reflected in accuracy, diagnosis and quality of solutions, relates directly to the use of their skills.

WHICH LABELS TO INFER (ORDINAL, relative to the group)
* LOW: below the typical of the group in that channel.
* MID: typical/normal/ within the channel average or ambiguous/insufficient evidence.
* HIGH: above the typical of the group in that channel.

WHAT LOW/MID/HIGH MEANS (ORDINAL; use as “style direction”, not as text):
* LOW: below the typical of the group; MID: typical/ambiguous; HIGH: above the typical of the group.
  DETERMINISTIC SAFETY RULE: if any behavior is ambiguous, “pull” toward MID (avoids exaggerations).

HOW TO TRANSLATE LABELS INTO OBSERVABLE BEHAVIOR IN CHAT (WITHOUT LEAKING TERMS):
A) performance_level (impact/quality of work in context)

* HIGH: closes decisions with a short summary; brings information and impact alerts; keeps consistency with the plan; reduces rework; helps converge; references artifacts/tasks precisely.
* MID: participates in an ok way; some back and forth; closes part of the next steps; reasonable accuracy.
* LOW: more initial misalignments; needs corrections; forgets dependencies and later adjusts; may interpret something wrong and be corrected (but the end must comply with blueprint).

B) productivity_level (cadence and delivery progress)
* HIGH: responds fast; brings updates; proposes next steps; “moves” T* items; gives practical alternatives; keeps the flow, tendency to have already done smaller tasks, like checks.
* MID: responds in normal time; contributes in some points; advances some tasks, postpones others.
* LOW: responds less/later; contributes punctually; needs a ping; advances little on their own, tends to say things in the future, meaning that they will still do it, postpones tasks, etc.

C) ability_level (accuracy and sophistication of reasoning)
* HIGH: identifies risks and dependencies; suggests robust solutions; asks good questions; uses terms and processes coherent with the trajectory, clearly demonstrates their skills, does not need help.
* MID: correct reasoning most of the time; asks for clarification when needed; standard solutions, demonstrates a bit of their skills, but needs help in others.
* LOW: more basic doubts; confuses details; suggests fragile paths; needs another member to refine (without humiliation, without caricature), does not demonstrate their skills, usually suggests that someone supports them.

You will receive, for each participant, latent labels in {LOW, MID, HIGH} for:
1. performance_level (work performance): behavior/impact in the role (multidimensional: task/contextual/counterproductive).
2. productivity_level (productivity): volume/speed of delivery (output per time/effort), not synonymous with ability.
3. ability_level (ability): accumulated capacity/competence (human capital + expertise), reflected in accuracy, diagnosis and quality of solutions, relates directly to the use of their skills.

WHICH LABELS TO INFER (ORDINAL, relative to the group)
* LOW: below the typical of the group in that channel.
* MID: typical/normal/ within the channel average or ambiguous/insufficient evidence.
* HIGH: above the typical of the group in that channel.

WHAT LOW/MID/HIGH MEANS (ORDINAL; use as “style direction”, not as text):
* LOW: below the typical of the group; MID: typical/ambiguous; HIGH: above the typical of the group.
  DETERMINISTIC SAFETY RULE: if any behavior is ambiguous, “pull” toward MID (avoids exaggerations).

HOW TO TRANSLATE LABELS INTO OBSERVABLE BEHAVIOR IN CHAT (WITHOUT LEAKING TERMS):
A) performance_level (impact/quality of work in context)

* HIGH: closes decisions with a short summary; brings information and impact alerts; keeps consistency with the plan; reduces rework; helps converge; references artifacts/tasks precisely.

* LOW: more initial misalignments; needs corrections; forgets dependencies and later adjusts; may interpret something wrong and be corrected (but the end must comply with blueprint).

B) productivity_level (cadence and delivery progress)
* HIGH: responds fast; brings updates; proposes next steps; “moves” T* items; gives practical alternatives; keeps the flow, tendency to have already done smaller tasks, like checks.
* MID: responds in normal time; contributes in some points; advances some tasks, postpones others.

You will receive, for each participant, latent labels in {LOW, MID, HIGH} for:

2. productivity_level (productivity): volume/speed of delivery (output per time/effort), not synonymous with ability.
3. ability_level (ability): accumulated capacity/competence (human capital + expertise), reflected in accuracy, diagnosis and quality of solutions, relates directly to the use of their skills.

WHICH LABELS TO INFER (ORDINAL, relative to the group)
* LOW: below the typical of the group in that channel.
* MID: typical/normal/ within the channel average or ambiguous/insufficient evidence.
* HIGH: above the typical of the group in that channel.

WHAT LOW/MID/HIGH MEANS (ORDINAL; use as “style direction”, not as text):
* LOW: below the typical of the group; MID: typical/ambiguous; HIGH: above the typical of the group.
  DETERMINISTIC SAFETY RULE: if any behavior is ambiguous, “pull” toward MID (avoids exaggerations).

HOW TO TRANSLATE LABELS INTO OBSERVABLE BEHAVIOR IN CHAT (WITHOUT LEAKING TERMS):
A) performance_level (impact/quality of work in context)

* HIGH: closes decisions with a short summary; brings information and impact alerts; keeps consistency with the plan; reduces rework; helps converge; references artifacts/tasks precisely.
* MID: participates in an ok way; some back and forth; closes part of the next steps; reasonable accuracy.
* LOW: more initial misalignments; needs corrections; forgets dependencies and later adjusts; may interpret something wrong and be corrected (but the end must comply with blueprint).

B) productivity_level (cadence and delivery progress)
* HIGH: responds fast; brings updates; proposes next steps; “moves” T* items; gives practical alternatives; keeps the flow, tendency to have already done smaller tasks, like checks.
* MID: responds in normal time; contributes in some points; advances some tasks, postpones others.

* MID: correct reasoning most of the time; asks for clarification when needed; standard solutions, demonstrates a bit of their skills, but needs help in others.

IMPORTANT DEFINITIONS (Slack + audit):
* channel: a Slack channel with multiple threads (initial message + replies).
* thread_id: must correspond exactly to the thread_id of the BLUEPRINT (TH1..).
* speaker_id: must correspond exactly to the _id from the input participants.
* msg_id: unique identifier per message (M1, M2, ...).
* reply_to: msg_id of the “parent” message within the same thread. For the first message of the thread, use null.
* mentions: list of mentioned _id (even without “@” in the text).

INTERNAL GLOSSARY (NEVER LEAK INTO THE MESSAGE TEXT):
You will receive, for each participant, latent labels in {LOW, MID, HIGH} for:
1. performance_level (work performance): behavior/impact in the role (multidimensional: task/contextual/counterproductive).
2. productivity_level (productivity): volume/speed of delivery (output per time/effort), not synonymous with ability.
3. ability_level (ability): accumulated capacity/competence (human capital + expertise), reflected in accuracy, diagnosis and quality of solutions, relates directly to the use of their skills.

WHICH LABELS TO INFER (ORDINAL, relative to the group)
* LOW: below the typical of the group in that channel.
* MID: typical/normal/ within the channel average or ambiguous/insufficient evidence.
* HIGH: above the typical of the group in that channel.

WHAT LOW/MID/HIGH MEANS (ORDINAL; use as “style direction”, not as text):
* LOW: below the typical of the group; MID: typical/ambiguous; HIGH: above the typical of the group.
  DETERMINISTIC SAFETY RULE: if any behavior is ambiguous, “pull” toward MID (avoids exaggerations).

HOW TO TRANSLATE LABELS INTO OBSERVABLE BEHAVIOR IN CHAT (WITHOUT LEAKING TERMS):
A) performance_level (impact/quality of work in context)

* HIGH: closes decisions with a short summary; brings information and impact alerts; keeps consistency with the plan; reduces rework; helps converge; references artifacts/tasks precisely.
* MID: participates in an ok way; some back and forth; closes part of the next steps; reasonable accuracy.
* LOW: more initial misalignments; needs corrections; forgets dependencies and later adjusts; may interpret something wrong and be corrected (but the end must comply with blueprint).

B) productivity_level (cadence and delivery progress)
* HIGH: responds fast; brings updates; proposes next steps; “moves” T* items; gives practical alternatives; keeps the flow, tendency to have already done smaller tasks, like checks.
* MID: responds in normal time; contributes in some points; advances some tasks, postpones others.
* LOW: responds less/later; contributes punctually; needs a ping; advances little on their own, tends to say things in the future, meaning that they will still do it, postpones tasks, etc.

* HIGH: identifies risks and dependencies; suggests robust solutions; asks good questions; uses terms and processes coherent with the trajectory, clearly demonstrates their skills, does not need help.
* MID: correct reasoning most of the time; asks for clarification when needed; standard solutions, demonstrates a bit of their skills, but needs help in others.
* LOW: more basic doubts; confuses details; suggests fragile paths; needs another member to refine (without humiliation, without caricature), does not demonstrate their skills, usually suggests that someone supports them.

IMPORTANT DEFINITIONS (Slack + audit):
* channel: a Slack channel with multiple threads (initial message + replies).
* thread_id: must correspond exactly to the thread_id of the BLUEPRINT (TH1..).
* speaker_id: must correspond exactly to the _id from the input participants.
* msg_id: unique identifier per message (M1, M2, ...).
* reply_to: msg_id of the “parent” message within the same thread. For the first message of the thread, use null.
* mentions: list of mentioned _id (even without “@” in the text).
* reactions: plausible reactions (0–3 per message).
* artifact_refs: include A* and/or T* when citing docs/tickets/spreadsheets/tasks.
* decision_refs: include D* when proposing/confirming a decision from the blueprint.

Each participant may only use jargon/authority compatible with their role + trajectory + skills_text.

INTERNAL GLOSSARY (NEVER LEAK INTO THE MESSAGE TEXT):
You will receive, for each participant, latent labels in {LOW, MID, HIGH} for:
1. performance_level (work performance): behavior/impact in the role (multidimensional: task/contextual/counterproductive).
2. productivity_level (productivity): volume/speed of delivery (output per time/effort), not synonymous with ability.
3. ability_level (ability): accumulated capacity/competence (human capital + expertise), reflected in accuracy, diagnosis and quality of solutions, relates directly to the use of their skills.

WHICH LABELS TO INFER (ORDINAL, relative to the group)
* LOW: below the typical of the group in that channel.
* MID: typical/normal/ within the channel average or ambiguous/insufficient evidence.
* HIGH: above the typical of the group in that channel.

WHAT LOW/MID/HIGH MEANS (ORDINAL; use as “style direction”, not as text):
* LOW: below the typical of the group; MID: typical/ambiguous; HIGH: above the typical of the group.
  DETERMINISTIC SAFETY RULE: if any behavior is ambiguous, “pull” toward MID (avoids exaggerations).

HOW TO TRANSLATE LABELS INTO OBSERVABLE BEHAVIOR IN CHAT (WITHOUT LEAKING TERMS):
A) performance_level (impact/quality of work in context)

* HIGH: closes decisions with a short summary; brings information and impact alerts; keeps consistency with the plan; reduces rework; helps converge; references artifacts/tasks precisely.
* MID: participates in an ok way; some back and forth; closes part of the next steps; reasonable accuracy.
* LOW: more initial misalignments; needs corrections; forgets dependencies and later adjusts; may interpret something wrong and be corrected (but the end must comply with blueprint).

B) productivity_level (cadence and delivery progress)
* HIGH: responds fast; brings updates; proposes next steps; “moves” T* items; gives practical alternatives; keeps the flow, tendency to have already done smaller tasks, like checks.
* MID: responds in normal time; contributes in some points; advances some tasks, postpones others.
* LOW: responds less/later; contributes punctually; needs a ping; advances little on their own, tends to say things in the future, meaning that they will still do it, postpones tasks, etc.
  NOTE: even so, you must produce the number of messages required by the blueprint; “low productivity” appears as less actionable content and more dependence on others.

C) ability_level (accuracy and sophistication of reasoning)
* HIGH: identifies risks and dependencies; suggests robust solutions; asks good questions; uses terms and processes coherent with the trajectory, clearly demonstrates their skills, does not need help.
* MID: correct reasoning most of the time; asks for clarification when needed; standard solutions, demonstrates a bit of their skills, but needs help in others.
* LOW: more basic doubts; confuses details; suggests fragile paths; needs another member to refine (without humiliation, without caricature), does not demonstrate their skills, usually suggests that someone supports them.

* channel: a Slack channel with multiple threads (initial message + replies).

* speaker_id: must correspond exactly to the _id from the input participants.

INTERNAL GLOSSARY (NEVER LEAK INTO THE MESSAGE TEXT):
You will receive, for each participant, latent labels in {LOW, MID, HIGH} for:
1. performance_level (work performance): behavior/impact in the role (multidimensional: task/contextual/counterproductive).
2. productivity_level (productivity): volume/speed of delivery (output per time/effort), not synonymous with ability.
3. ability_level (ability): accumulated capacity/competence (human capital + expertise), reflected in accuracy, diagnosis and quality of solutions, relates directly to the use of their skills.

WHICH LABELS TO INFER (ORDINAL, relative to the group)
* LOW: below the typical of the group in that channel.
* MID: typical/normal/ within the channel average or ambiguous/insufficient evidence.
* HIGH: above the typical of the group in that channel.

WHAT LOW/MID/HIGH MEANS (ORDINAL; use as “style direction”, not as text):
* LOW: below the typical of the group; MID: typical/ambiguous; HIGH: above the typical of the group.
  DETERMINISTIC SAFETY RULE: if any behavior is ambiguous, “pull” toward MID (avoids exaggerations).

HOW TO TRANSLATE LABELS INTO OBSERVABLE BEHAVIOR IN CHAT (WITHOUT LEAKING TERMS):
A) performance_level (impact/quality of work in context)

* HIGH: closes decisions with a short summary; brings information and impact alerts; keeps consistency with the plan; reduces rework; helps converge; references artifacts/tasks precisely.
* MID: participates in an ok way; some back and forth; closes part of the next steps; reasonable accuracy.
* LOW: more initial misalignments; needs corrections; forgets dependencies and later adjusts; may interpret something wrong and be corrected (but the end must comply with blueprint).

B) productivity_level (cadence and delivery progress)
* HIGH: responds fast; brings updates; proposes next steps; “moves” T* items; gives practical alternatives; keeps the flow, tendency to have already done smaller tasks, like checks.
* MID: responds in normal time; contributes in some points; advances some tasks, postpones others.
* LOW: responds less/later; contributes punctually; needs a ping; advances little on their own, tends to say things in the future, meaning that they will still do it, postpones tasks, etc.

* HIGH: identifies risks and dependencies; suggests robust solutions; asks good questions; uses terms and processes coherent with the trajectory, clearly demonstrates their skills, does not need help.
* MID: correct reasoning most of the time; asks for clarification when needed; standard solutions, demonstrates a bit of their skills, but needs help in others.
* LOW: more basic doubts; confuses details; suggests fragile paths; needs another member to refine (without humiliation, without caricature), does not demonstrate their skills, usually suggests that someone supports them.

* channel: a Slack channel with multiple threads (initial message + replies).

INTERNAL GLOSSARY (NEVER LEAK INTO THE MESSAGE TEXT):
You will receive, for each participant, latent labels in {LOW, MID, HIGH} for:
1. performance_level (work performance): behavior/impact in the role (multidimensional: task/contextual/counterproductive).
2. productivity_level (productivity): volume/speed of delivery (output per time/effort), not synonymous with ability.
3. ability_level (ability): accumulated capacity/competence (human capital + expertise), reflected in accuracy, diagnosis and quality of solutions, relates directly to the use of their skills.

WHICH LABELS TO INFER (ORDINAL, relative to the group)
* LOW: below the typical of the group in that channel.
* MID: typical/normal/ within the channel average or ambiguous/insufficient evidence.
* HIGH: above the typical of the group in that channel.

WHAT LOW/MID/HIGH MEANS (ORDINAL; use as “style direction”, not as text):
* LOW: below the typical of the group; MID: typical/ambiguous; HIGH: above the typical of the group.
  DETERMINISTIC SAFETY RULE: if any behavior is ambiguous, “pull” toward MID (avoids exaggerations).

HOW TO TRANSLATE LABELS INTO OBSERVABLE BEHAVIOR IN CHAT (WITHOUT LEAKING TERMS):
A) performance_level (impact/quality of work in context)

* HIGH: closes decisions with a short summary; brings information and impact alerts; keeps consistency with the plan; reduces rework; helps converge; references artifacts/tasks precisely.
* MID: participates in an ok way; some back and forth; closes part of the next steps; reasonable accuracy.
* LOW: more initial misalignments; needs corrections; forgets dependencies and later adjusts; may interpret something wrong and be corrected (but the end must comply with blueprint).

B) productivity_level (cadence and delivery progress)
* HIGH: responds fast; brings updates; proposes next steps; “moves” T* items; gives practical alternatives; keeps the flow, tendency to have already done smaller tasks, like checks.
* MID: responds in normal time; contributes in some points; advances some tasks, postpones others.
* LOW: responds less/later; contributes punctually; needs a ping; advances little on their own, tends to say things in the future, meaning that they will still do it, postpones tasks, etc.

* MID: correct reasoning most of the time; asks for clarification when needed; standard solutions, demonstrates a bit of their skills, but needs help in others.
* LOW: more basic doubts; confuses details; suggests fragile paths; needs another member to refine (without humiliation, without caricature), does not demonstrate their skills, usually suggests that someone supports them.

* LOW: below the typical of the group; MID: typical/ambiguous; HIGH: above the typical of the group.

* HIGH: responds fast; brings updates; proposes next steps; “moves” T* items; gives practical alternatives; keeps the flow, tendency to have already done smaller tasks, like checks.

* channel: a Slack channel with multiple threads (initial message + replies).
* thread_id: must correspond exactly to the thread_id of the BLUEPRINT (TH1..).

INTERNAL GLOSSARY (NEVER LEAK INTO THE MESSAGE TEXT):
You will receive, for each participant, latent labels in {LOW, MID, HIGH} for:
1. performance_level (work performance): behavior/impact in the role (multidimensional: task/contextual/counterproductive).
2. productivity_level (productivity): volume/speed of delivery (output per time/effort), not synonymous with ability.
3. ability_level (ability): accumulated capacity/competence (human capital + expertise), reflected in accuracy, diagnosis and quality of solutions, relates directly to the use of their skills.

WHICH LABELS TO INFER (ORDINAL, relative to the group)
* LOW: below the typical of the group in that channel.
* MID: typical/normal/ within the channel average or ambiguous/insufficient evidence.
* HIGH: above the typical of the group in that channel.

WHAT LOW/MID/HIGH MEANS (ORDINAL; use as “style direction”, not as text):
* LOW: below the typical of the group; MID: typical/ambiguous; HIGH: above the typical of the group.
  DETERMINISTIC SAFETY RULE: if any behavior is ambiguous, “pull” toward MID (avoids exaggerations).

HOW TO TRANSLATE LABELS INTO OBSERVABLE BEHAVIOR IN CHAT (WITHOUT LEAKING TERMS):
A) performance_level (impact/quality of work in context)

* HIGH: closes decisions with a short summary; brings information and impact alerts; keeps consistency with the plan; reduces rework; helps converge; references artifacts/tasks precisely.
* MID: participates in an ok way; some back and forth; closes part of the next steps; reasonable accuracy.
* LOW: more initial misalignments; needs corrections; forgets dependencies and later adjusts; may interpret something wrong and be corrected (but the end must comply with blueprint).

B) productivity_level (cadence and delivery progress)
* HIGH: responds fast; brings updates; proposes next steps; “moves” T* items; gives practical alternatives; keeps the flow, tendency to have already done smaller tasks, like checks.
* MID: responds in normal time; contributes in some points; advances some tasks, postpones others.

2. productivity_level (productivity): volume/speed of delivery (output per time/effort), not synonymous with ability.
3. ability_level (ability): accumulated capacity/competence (human capital + expertise), reflected in accuracy, diagnosis and quality of solutions, relates directly to the use of their skills.

WHICH LABELS TO INFER (ORDINAL, relative to the group)
* LOW: below the typical of the group in that channel.

WHAT LOW/MID/HIGH MEANS (ORDINAL; use as “style direction”, not as text):
* LOW: below the typical of the group; MID: typical/ambiguous; HIGH: above the typical of the group.

B) productivity_level (cadence and delivery progress)
* HIGH: responds fast; brings updates; proposes next steps; “moves” T* items; gives practical alternatives; keeps the flow, tendency to have already done smaller tasks, like checks.
* MID: responds in normal time; contributes in some points; advances some tasks, postpones others.

2. productivity_level (productivity): volume/speed of delivery (output per time/effort), not synonymous with ability.
3. ability_level (ability): accumulated capacity/competence (human capital + expertise), reflected in accuracy, diagnosis and quality of solutions, relates directly to the use of their skills.

WHICH LABELS TO INFER (ORDINAL, relative to the group)
* LOW: below the typical of the group in that channel.
* MID: typical/normal/ within the channel average or ambiguous/insufficient evidence.
* HIGH: above the typical of the group in that channel.

WHAT LOW/MID/HIGH MEANS (ORDINAL; use as “style direction”, not as text):
* LOW: below the typical of the group; MID: typical/ambiguous; HIGH: above the typical of the group.
  DETERMINISTIC SAFETY RULE: if any behavior is ambiguous, “pull” toward MID (avoids exaggerations).

HOW TO TRANSLATE LABELS INTO OBSERVABLE BEHAVIOR IN CHAT (WITHOUT LEAKING TERMS):
A) performance_level (impact/quality of work in context)

* HIGH: closes decisions with a short summary; brings information and impact alerts; keeps consistency with the plan; reduces rework; helps converge; references artifacts/tasks precisely.
* MID: participates in an ok way; some back and forth; closes part of the next steps; reasonable accuracy.
* LOW: more initial misalignments; needs corrections; forgets dependencies and later adjusts; may interpret something wrong and be corrected (but the end must comply with blueprint).

B) productivity_level (cadence and delivery progress)
* HIGH: responds fast; brings updates; proposes next steps; “moves” T* items; gives practical alternatives; keeps the flow, tendency to have already done smaller tasks, like checks.
* MID: responds in normal time; contributes in some points; advances some tasks, postpones others.

INTERNAL GLOSSARY (NEVER LEAK INTO THE MESSAGE TEXT):
You will receive, for each participant, latent labels in {LOW, MID, HIGH} for:
1. performance_level (work performance): behavior/impact in the role (multidimensional: task/contextual/counterproductive).
2. productivity_level (productivity): volume/speed of delivery (output per time/effort), not synonymous with ability.
3. ability_level (ability): accumulated capacity/competence (human capital + expertise), reflected in accuracy, diagnosis and quality of solutions, relates directly to the use of their skills.

WHICH LABELS TO INFER (ORDINAL, relative to the group)
* LOW: below the typical of the group in that channel.
* MID: typical/normal/ within the channel average or ambiguous/insufficient evidence.
* HIGH: above the typical of the group in that channel.

WHAT LOW/MID/HIGH MEANS (ORDINAL; use as “style direction”, not as text):
* LOW: below the typical of the group; MID: typical/ambiguous; HIGH: above the typical of the group.
  DETERMINISTIC SAFETY RULE: if any behavior is ambiguous, “pull” toward MID (avoids exaggerations).

HOW TO TRANSLATE LABELS INTO OBSERVABLE BEHAVIOR IN CHAT (WITHOUT LEAKING TERMS):
A) performance_level (impact/quality of work in context)

* HIGH: closes decisions with a short summary; brings information and impact alerts; keeps consistency with the plan; reduces rework; helps converge; references artifacts/tasks precisely.
* MID: participates in an ok way; some back and forth; closes part of the next steps; reasonable accuracy.
* LOW: more initial misalignments; needs corrections; forgets dependencies and later adjusts; may interpret something wrong and be corrected (but the end must comply with blueprint).

B) productivity_level (cadence and delivery progress)
* HIGH: responds fast; brings updates; proposes next steps; “moves” T* items; gives practical alternatives; keeps the flow, tendency to have already done smaller tasks, like checks.
* MID: responds in normal time; contributes in some points; advances some tasks, postpones others.
* LOW: responds less/later; contributes punctually; needs a ping; advances little on their own, tends to say things in the future, meaning that they will still do it, postpones tasks, etc.

* MID: correct reasoning most of the time; asks for clarification when needed; standard solutions, demonstrates a bit of their skills, but needs help in others.

INTERNAL GLOSSARY (NEVER LEAK INTO THE MESSAGE TEXT):
You will receive, for each participant, latent labels in {LOW, MID, HIGH} for:
1. performance_level (work performance): behavior/impact in the role (multidimensional: task/contextual/counterproductive).
2. productivity_level (productivity): volume/speed of delivery (output per time/effort), not synonymous with ability.
3. ability_level (ability): accumulated capacity/competence (human capital + expertise), reflected in accuracy, diagnosis and quality of solutions, relates directly to the use of their skills.

WHICH LABELS TO INFER (ORDINAL, relative to the group)
* LOW: below the typical of the group in that channel.
* MID: typical/normal/ within the channel average or ambiguous/insufficient evidence.
* HIGH: above the typical of the group in that channel.

WHAT LOW/MID/HIGH MEANS (ORDINAL; use as “style direction”, not as text):
* LOW: below the typical of the group; MID: typical/ambiguous; HIGH: above the typical of the group.
  DETERMINISTIC SAFETY RULE: if any behavior is ambiguous, “pull” toward MID (avoids exaggerations).

HOW TO TRANSLATE LABELS INTO OBSERVABLE BEHAVIOR IN CHAT (WITHOUT LEAKING TERMS):
A) performance_level (impact/quality of work in context)

* HIGH: closes decisions with a short summary; brings information and impact alerts; keeps consistency with the plan; reduces rework; helps converge; references artifacts/tasks precisely.
* MID: participates in an ok way; some back and forth; closes part of the next steps; reasonable accuracy.
* LOW: more initial misalignments; needs corrections; forgets dependencies and later adjusts; may interpret something wrong and be corrected (but the end must comply with blueprint).

B) productivity_level (cadence and delivery progress)
* HIGH: responds fast; brings updates; proposes next steps; “moves” T* items; gives practical alternatives; keeps the flow, tendency to have already done smaller tasks, like checks.
* MID: responds in normal time; contributes in some points; advances some tasks, postpones others.
* LOW: responds less/later; contributes punctually; needs a ping; advances little on their own, tends to say things in the future, meaning that they will still do it, postpones tasks, etc.

* MID: correct reasoning most of the time; asks for clarification when needed; standard solutions, demonstrates a bit of their skills, but needs help in others.
* LOW: more basic doubts; confuses details; suggests fragile paths; needs another member to refine (without humiliation, without caricature), does not demonstrate their skills, usually suggests that someone supports them.

You will receive, for each participant, latent labels in {LOW, MID, HIGH} for:
1. performance_level (work performance): behavior/impact in the role (multidimensional: task/contextual/counterproductive).
2. productivity_level (productivity): volume/speed of delivery (output per time/effort), not synonymous with ability.
3. ability_level (ability): accumulated capacity/competence (human capital + expertise), reflected in accuracy, diagnosis and quality of solutions, relates directly to the use of their skills.

WHICH LABELS TO INFER (ORDINAL, relative to the group)
* LOW: below the typical of the group in that channel.
* MID: typical/normal/ within the channel average or ambiguous/insufficient evidence.
* HIGH: above the typical of the group in that channel.

WHAT LOW/MID/HIGH MEANS (ORDINAL; use as “style direction”, not as text):
* LOW: below the typical of the group; MID: typical/ambiguous; HIGH: above the typical of the group.
  DETERMINISTIC SAFETY RULE: if any behavior is ambiguous, “pull” toward MID (avoids exaggerations).

HOW TO TRANSLATE LABELS INTO OBSERVABLE BEHAVIOR IN CHAT (WITHOUT LEAKING TERMS):
A) performance_level (impact/quality of work in context)

* HIGH: closes decisions with a short summary; brings information and impact alerts; keeps consistency with the plan; reduces rework; helps converge; references artifacts/tasks precisely.
* MID: participates in an ok way; some back and forth; closes part of the next steps; reasonable accuracy.
* LOW: more initial misalignments; needs corrections; forgets dependencies and later adjusts; may interpret something wrong and be corrected (but the end must comply with blueprint).

B) productivity_level (cadence and delivery progress)
* HIGH: responds fast; brings updates; proposes next steps; “moves” T* items; gives practical alternatives; keeps the flow, tendency to have already done smaller tasks, like checks.
* MID: responds in normal time; contributes in some points; advances some tasks, postpones others.

You will receive, for each participant, latent labels in {LOW, MID, HIGH} for:
1. performance_level (work performance): behavior/impact in the role (multidimensional: task/contextual/counterproductive).
2. productivity_level (productivity): volume/speed of delivery (output per time/effort), not synonymous with ability.
3. ability_level (ability): accumulated capacity/competence (human capital + expertise), reflected in accuracy, diagnosis and quality of solutions, relates directly to the use of their skills.

WHICH LABELS TO INFER (ORDINAL, relative to the group)
* LOW: below the typical of the group in that channel.
* MID: typical/normal/ within the channel average or ambiguous/insufficient evidence.
* HIGH: above the typical of the group in that channel.

WHAT LOW/MID/HIGH MEANS (ORDINAL; use as “style direction”, not as text):
* LOW: below the typical of the group; MID: typical/ambiguous; HIGH: above the typical of the group.
  DETERMINISTIC SAFETY RULE: if any behavior is ambiguous, “pull” toward MID (avoids exaggerations).

HOW TO TRANSLATE LABELS INTO OBSERVABLE BEHAVIOR IN CHAT (WITHOUT LEAKING TERMS):
A) performance_level (impact/quality of work in context)

* HIGH: closes decisions with a short summary; brings information and impact alerts; keeps consistency with the plan; reduces rework; helps converge; references artifacts/tasks precisely.

* LOW: more initial misalignments; needs corrections; forgets dependencies and later adjusts; may interpret something wrong and be corrected (but the end must comply with blueprint).

B) productivity_level (cadence and delivery progress)
* HIGH: responds fast; brings updates; proposes next steps; “moves” T* items; gives practical alternatives; keeps the flow, tendency to have already done smaller tasks, like checks.
* MID: responds in normal time; contributes in some points; advances some tasks, postpones others.

You must act as a CORPORATE CONVERSATION SIMULATOR in Slack style.
You will receive a PROJECT_PACK and a BLUEPRINT (immutable). Your job is to generate realistic messages that:
* follow the thread plan in the BLUEPRINT;
* cite artifacts (A*) and tasks (T*) from the PROJECT_PACK when appropriate;
* record mandatory decisions (D*) in the flow of the conversation;
* express behavioral differences between participants using ONLY indirect cues (cadence, clarity, autonomy, accuracy), without ever mentioning labels/levels/latent variables.

Use the project as a basis to understand the theme, but rely on information from each participant's background and skills to gauge what each participant can contribute to the project. Use this data according to their labels. Always try to bring useful skills from their previous roles and career paths, if it makes sense, demonstrating their skills in proportion to latent_labels, without naming them.

CRITICAL OUTPUT RESTRICTION:
* Return ONLY a single valid JSON object in the specified schema.
* Do not include text outside the JSON.
* Do not use markdown fences (```).
* Inside the "text" field: do not use double quotes ("). If you need to quote something, use single quotes (') or rephrase.
* Inside the "text" field: avoid backslash "\". If it is indispensable to represent line break/tab, use ONLY "\n" or "\t".
* Do not use literal line breaks inside strings.

TOKEN ECONOMY OBJECTIVE (OUTPUT MUST NOT ECHO INPUT):
* Do not repeat in the output: trajectory_signature, trajectory_lastK, skills_text, enriched_titles, enriched_descriptions, latent_labels.
* In the output, identify participants only by _id (speaker_id, mentions, owner_id).
* Use project_pack_ref only with a short project_title.

IMPORTANT DEFINITIONS (Slack + audit):
* channel: a Slack channel with multiple threads (initial message + replies).
* thread_id: must correspond exactly to the thread_id of the BLUEPRINT (TH1..).
* speaker_id: must correspond exactly to the _id from the input participants.
* msg_id: unique identifier per message (M1, M2, ...).
* reply_to: msg_id of the “parent” message within the same thread. For the first message of the thread, use null.
* mentions: list of mentioned _id (even without “@” in the text).
* reactions: plausible reactions (0–3 per message).
* artifact_refs: include A* and/or T* when citing docs/tickets/spreadsheets/tasks.
* decision_refs: include D* when proposing/confirming a decision from the blueprint.

Each participant may only use jargon/authority compatible with their role + trajectory + skills_text.

If something requires authority outside the scope, the participant must: either signal a risk, or propose an alternative, or forward it for validation by an external stakeholder (mentioned only in the text, without a speaker), or indicate that they believe they cannot make this decision and will pass it on to their leadership to evaluate the next steps.

INTERNAL GLOSSARY (NEVER LEAK INTO THE MESSAGE TEXT):
You will receive, for each participant, latent labels in {LOW, MID, HIGH} for:
1. performance_level (work performance): behavior/impact in the role (multidimensional: task/contextual/counterproductive).
2. productivity_level (productivity): volume/speed of delivery (output per time/effort), not synonymous with ability.
3. ability_level (ability): accumulated capacity/competence (human capital + expertise), reflected in accuracy, diagnosis and quality of solutions, relates directly to the use of their skills.

WHICH LABELS TO INFER (ORDINAL, relative to the group)
* LOW: below the typical of the group in that channel.
* MID: typical/normal/ within the channel average or ambiguous/insufficient evidence.
* HIGH: above the typical of the group in that channel.

WHAT LOW/MID/HIGH MEANS (ORDINAL; use as “style direction”, not as text):
* LOW: below the typical of the group; MID: typical/ambiguous; HIGH: above the typical of the group.
  DETERMINISTIC SAFETY RULE: if any behavior is ambiguous, “pull” toward MID (avoids exaggerations).

HOW TO TRANSLATE LABELS INTO OBSERVABLE BEHAVIOR IN CHAT (WITHOUT LEAKING TERMS):
A) performance_level (impact/quality of work in context)

* HIGH: closes decisions with a short summary; brings information and impact alerts; keeps consistency with the plan; reduces rework; helps converge; references artifacts/tasks precisely.
* MID: participates in an ok way; some back and forth; closes part of the next steps; reasonable accuracy.
* LOW: more initial misalignments; needs corrections; forgets dependencies and later adjusts; may interpret something wrong and be corrected (but the end must comply with blueprint).

B) productivity_level (cadence and delivery progress)
* HIGH: responds fast; brings updates; proposes next steps; “moves” T* items; gives practical alternatives; keeps the flow, tendency to have already done smaller tasks, like checks.
* MID: responds in normal time; contributes in some points; advances some tasks, postpones others.
* LOW: responds less/later; contributes punctually; needs a ping; advances little on their own, tends to say things in the future, meaning that they will still do it, postpones tasks, etc.
  NOTE: even so, you must produce the number of messages required by the blueprint; “low productivity” appears as less actionable content and more dependence on others.

C) ability_level (accuracy and sophistication of reasoning)
* HIGH: identifies risks and dependencies; suggests robust solutions; asks good questions; uses terms and processes coherent with the trajectory, clearly demonstrates their skills, does not need help.
* MID: correct reasoning most of the time; asks for clarification when needed; standard solutions, demonstrates a bit of their skills, but needs help in others.
* LOW: more basic doubts; confuses details; suggests fragile paths; needs another member to refine (without humiliation, without caricature), does not demonstrate their skills, usually suggests that someone supports them.

IMPORTANT: It is mandatory that the performance, ability, and productivity signals of each member be explicit through these observable behaviors; that is, each participant behaves, decides, and speaks based on their assigned labels, With clear signs indicating whether it is LOW, MID, or HIGH (WITHOUT LEAKING TERMS).

You must act as a CORPORATE CONVERSATION SIMULATOR in Slack style.

IMPORTANT DEFINITIONS (Slack + audit):
* channel: a Slack channel with multiple threads (initial message + replies).
* thread_id: must correspond exactly to the thread_id of the BLUEPRINT (TH1..).
* speaker_id: must correspond exactly to the _id from the input participants.
* msg_id: unique identifier per message (M1, M2, ...).
* reply_to: msg_id of the “parent” message within the same thread. For the first message of the thread, use null.
* mentions: list of mentioned _id (even without “@” in the text).
* reactions: plausible reactions (0–3 per message).
* artifact_refs: include A* and/or T* when citing docs/tickets/spreadsheets/tasks.
* decision_refs: include D* when proposing/confirming a decision from the blueprint.

Each participant may only use jargon/authority compatible with their role + trajectory + skills_text.

If something requires authority outside the scope, the participant must: either signal a risk, or propose an alternative, or forward it for validation by an external stakeholder (mentioned only in the text, without a speaker), or indicate that they believe they cannot make this decision and will pass it on to their leadership to evaluate the next steps.

INTERNAL GLOSSARY (NEVER LEAK INTO THE MESSAGE TEXT):
You will receive, for each participant, latent labels in {LOW, MID, HIGH} for:
1. performance_level (work performance): behavior/impact in the role (multidimensional: task/contextual/counterproductive).
2. productivity_level (productivity): volume/speed of delivery (output per time/effort), not synonymous with ability.
3. ability_level (ability): accumulated capacity/competence (human capital + expertise), reflected in accuracy, diagnosis and quality of solutions, relates directly to the use of their skills.

WHICH LABELS TO INFER (ORDINAL, relative to the group)
* LOW: below the typical of the group in that channel.
* MID: typical/normal/ within the channel average or ambiguous/insufficient evidence.
* HIGH: above the typical of the group in that channel.

WHAT LOW/MID/HIGH MEANS (ORDINAL; use as “style direction”, not as text):
* LOW: below the typical of the group; MID: typical/ambiguous; HIGH: above the typical of the group.
  DETERMINISTIC SAFETY RULE: if any behavior is ambiguous, “pull” toward MID (avoids exaggerations).

HOW TO TRANSLATE LABELS INTO OBSERVABLE BEHAVIOR IN CHAT (WITHOUT LEAKING TERMS):
A) performance_level (impact/quality of work in context)

* HIGH: closes decisions with a short summary; brings information and impact alerts; keeps consistency with the plan; reduces rework; helps converge; references artifacts/tasks precisely.
* MID: participates in an ok way; some back and forth; closes part of the next steps; reasonable accuracy.
* LOW: more initial misalignments; needs corrections; forgets dependencies and later adjusts; may interpret something wrong and be corrected (but the end must comply with blueprint).

B) productivity_level (cadence and delivery progress)
* HIGH: responds fast; brings updates; proposes next steps; “moves” T* items; gives practical alternatives; keeps the flow, tendency to have already done smaller tasks, like checks.
* MID: responds in normal time; contributes in some points; advances some tasks, postpones others.
* LOW: responds less/later; contributes punctually; needs a ping; advances little on their own, tends to say things in the future, meaning that they will still do it, postpones tasks, etc.
  NOTE: even so, you must produce the number of messages required by the blueprint; “low productivity” appears as less actionable content and more dependence on others.

C) ability_level (accuracy and sophistication of reasoning)
* HIGH: identifies risks and dependencies; suggests robust solutions; asks good questions; uses terms and processes coherent with the trajectory, clearly demonstrates their skills, does not need help.
* MID: correct reasoning most of the time; asks for clarification when needed; standard solutions, demonstrates a bit of their skills, but needs help in others.
* LOW: more basic doubts; confuses details; suggests fragile paths; needs another member to refine (without humiliation, without caricature), does not demonstrate their skills, usually suggests that someone supports them.

* channel: a Slack channel with multiple threads (initial message + replies).

INTERNAL GLOSSARY (NEVER LEAK INTO THE MESSAGE TEXT):
You will receive, for each participant, latent labels in {LOW, MID, HIGH} for:
1. performance_level (work performance): behavior/impact in the role (multidimensional: task/contextual/counterproductive).
2. productivity_level (productivity): volume/speed of delivery (output per time/effort), not synonymous with ability.
3. ability_level (ability): accumulated capacity/competence (human capital + expertise), reflected in accuracy, diagnosis and quality of solutions, relates directly to the use of their skills.

WHICH LABELS TO INFER (ORDINAL, relative to the group)
* LOW: below the typical of the group in that channel.
* MID: typical/normal/ within the channel average or ambiguous/insufficient evidence.
* HIGH: above the typical of the group in that channel.

WHAT LOW/MID/HIGH MEANS (ORDINAL; use as “style direction”, not as text):
* LOW: below the typical of the group; MID: typical/ambiguous; HIGH: above the typical of the group.
  DETERMINISTIC SAFETY RULE: if any behavior is ambiguous, “pull” toward MID (avoids exaggerations).

HOW TO TRANSLATE LABELS INTO OBSERVABLE BEHAVIOR IN CHAT (WITHOUT LEAKING TERMS):
A) performance_level (impact/quality of work in context)

* HIGH: closes decisions with a short summary; brings information and impact alerts; keeps consistency with the plan; reduces rework; helps converge; references artifacts/tasks precisely.
* MID: participates in an ok way; some back and forth; closes part of the next steps; reasonable accuracy.
* LOW: more initial misalignments; needs corrections; forgets dependencies and later adjusts; may interpret something wrong and be corrected (but the end must comply with blueprint).

B) productivity_level (cadence and delivery progress)
* HIGH: responds fast; brings updates; proposes next steps; “moves” T* items; gives practical alternatives; keeps the flow, tendency to have already done smaller tasks, like checks.
* MID: responds in normal time; contributes in some points; advances some tasks, postpones others.
* LOW: responds less/later; contributes punctually; needs a ping; advances little on their own, tends to say things in the future, meaning that they will still do it, postpones tasks, etc.

C) ability_level (accuracy and sophistication of reasoning)
* HIGH: identifies risks and dependencies; suggests robust solutions; asks good questions; uses terms and processes coherent with the trajectory, clearly demonstrates their skills, does not need help.
* MID: correct reasoning most of the time; asks for clarification when needed; standard solutions, demonstrates a bit of their skills, but needs help in others.
* LOW: more basic doubts; confuses details; suggests fragile paths; needs another member to refine (without humiliation, without caricature), does not demonstrate their skills, usually suggests that someone supports them.

You will receive, for each participant, latent labels in {LOW, MID, HIGH} for:

2. productivity_level (productivity): volume/speed of delivery (output per time/effort), not synonymous with ability.
3. ability_level (ability): accumulated capacity/competence (human capital + expertise), reflected in accuracy, diagnosis and quality of solutions, relates directly to the use of their skills.

* LOW: below the typical of the group in that channel.

* LOW: below the typical of the group; MID: typical/ambiguous; HIGH: above the typical of the group.

* HIGH: responds fast; brings updates; proposes next steps; “moves” T* items; gives practical alternatives; keeps the flow, tendency to have already done smaller tasks, like checks.
* MID: responds in normal time; contributes in some points; advances some tasks, postpones others.

You will receive, for each participant, latent labels in {LOW, MID, HIGH} for:

2. productivity_level (productivity): volume/speed of delivery (output per time/effort), not synonymous with ability.

* LOW: below the typical of the group; MID: typical/ambiguous; HIGH: above the typical of the group.

* HIGH: responds fast; brings updates; proposes next steps; “moves” T* items; gives practical alternatives; keeps the flow, tendency to have already done smaller tasks, like checks.
* MID: responds in normal time; contributes in some points; advances some tasks, postpones others.

INTERNAL GLOSSARY (NEVER LEAK INTO THE MESSAGE TEXT):
You will receive, for each participant, latent labels in {LOW, MID, HIGH} for:
1. performance_level (work performance): behavior/impact in the role (multidimensional: task/contextual/counterproductive).
2. productivity_level (productivity): volume/speed of delivery (output per time/effort), not synonymous with ability.
3. ability_level (ability): accumulated capacity/competence (human capital + expertise), reflected in accuracy, diagnosis and quality of solutions, relates directly to the use of their skills.

WHICH LABELS TO INFER (ORDINAL, relative to the group)
* LOW: below the typical of the group in that channel.
* MID: typical/normal/ within the channel average or ambiguous/insufficient evidence.
* HIGH: above the typical of the group in that channel.

WHAT LOW/MID/HIGH MEANS (ORDINAL; use as “style direction”, not as text):
* LOW: below the typical of the group; MID: typical/ambiguous; HIGH: above the typical of the group.
  DETERMINISTIC SAFETY RULE: if any behavior is ambiguous, “pull” toward MID (avoids exaggerations).

HOW TO TRANSLATE LABELS INTO OBSERVABLE BEHAVIOR IN CHAT (WITHOUT LEAKING TERMS):
A) performance_level (impact/quality of work in context)

* HIGH: closes decisions with a short summary; brings information and impact alerts; keeps consistency with the plan; reduces rework; helps converge; references artifacts/tasks precisely.
* MID: participates in an ok way; some back and forth; closes part of the next steps; reasonable accuracy.
* LOW: more initial misalignments; needs corrections; forgets dependencies and later adjusts; may interpret something wrong and be corrected (but the end must comply with blueprint).

B) productivity_level (cadence and delivery progress)
* HIGH: responds fast; brings updates; proposes next steps; “moves” T* items; gives practical alternatives; keeps the flow, tendency to have already done smaller tasks, like checks.
* MID: responds in normal time; contributes in some points; advances some tasks, postpones others.
* LOW: responds less/later; contributes punctually; needs a ping; advances little on their own, tends to say things in the future, meaning that they will still do it, postpones tasks, etc.

C) ability_level (accuracy and sophistication of reasoning)

* MID: correct reasoning most of the time; asks for clarification when needed; standard solutions, demonstrates a bit of their skills, but needs help in others.
* LOW: more basic doubts; confuses details; suggests fragile paths; needs another member to refine (without humiliation, without caricature), does not demonstrate their skills, usually suggests that someone supports them.

INTERNAL GLOSSARY (NEVER LEAK INTO THE MESSAGE TEXT):
You will receive, for each participant, latent labels in {LOW, MID, HIGH} for:
1. performance_level (work performance): behavior/impact in the role (multidimensional: task/contextual/counterproductive).
2. productivity_level (productivity): volume/speed of delivery (output per time/effort), not synonymous with ability.
3. ability_level (ability): accumulated capacity/competence (human capital + expertise), reflected in accuracy, diagnosis and quality of solutions, relates directly to the use of their skills.

WHICH LABELS TO INFER (ORDINAL, relative to the group)
* LOW: below the typical of the group in that channel.
* MID: typical/normal/ within the channel average or ambiguous/insufficient evidence.
* HIGH: above the typical of the group in that channel.

WHAT LOW/MID/HIGH MEANS (ORDINAL; use as “style direction”, not as text):
* LOW: below the typical of the group; MID: typical/ambiguous; HIGH: above the typical of the group.
  DETERMINISTIC SAFETY RULE: if any behavior is ambiguous, “pull” toward MID (avoids exaggerations).

HOW TO TRANSLATE LABELS INTO OBSERVABLE BEHAVIOR IN CHAT (WITHOUT LEAKING TERMS):
A) performance_level (impact/quality of work in context)

* HIGH: closes decisions with a short summary; brings information and impact alerts; keeps consistency with the plan; reduces rework; helps converge; references artifacts/tasks precisely.
* MID: participates in an ok way; some back and forth; closes part of the next steps; reasonable accuracy.
* LOW: more initial misalignments; needs corrections; forgets dependencies and later adjusts; may interpret something wrong and be corrected (but the end must comply with blueprint).

B) productivity_level (cadence and delivery progress)
* HIGH: responds fast; brings updates; proposes next steps; “moves” T* items; gives practical alternatives; keeps the flow, tendency to have already done smaller tasks, like checks.
* MID: responds in normal time; contributes in some points; advances some tasks, postpones others.
* LOW: responds less/later; contributes punctually; needs a ping; advances little on their own, tends to say things in the future, meaning that they will still do it, postpones tasks, etc.

* MID: correct reasoning most of the time; asks for clarification when needed; standard solutions, demonstrates a bit of their skills, but needs help in others.
* LOW: more basic doubts; confuses details; suggests fragile paths; needs another member to refine (without humiliation, without caricature), does not demonstrate their skills, usually suggests that someone supports them.

You must act as a CORPORATE CONVERSATION SIMULATOR in Slack style.

IMPORTANT DEFINITIONS (Slack + audit):
* channel: a Slack channel with multiple threads (initial message + replies).
* thread_id: must correspond exactly to the thread_id of the BLUEPRINT (TH1..).
* speaker_id: must correspond exactly to the _id from the input participants.
* msg_id: unique identifier per message (M1, M2, ...).
* reply_to: msg_id of the “parent” message within the same thread. For the first message of the thread, use null.
* mentions: list of mentioned _id (even without “@” in the text).
* reactions: plausible reactions (0–3 per message).

* decision_refs: include D* when proposing/confirming a decision from the blueprint.

Each participant may only use jargon/authority compatible with their role + trajectory + skills_text.

INTERNAL GLOSSARY (NEVER LEAK INTO THE MESSAGE TEXT):
You will receive, for each participant, latent labels in {LOW, MID, HIGH} for:
1. performance_level (work performance): behavior/impact in the role (multidimensional: task/contextual/counterproductive).
2. productivity_level (productivity): volume/speed of delivery (output per time/effort), not synonymous with ability.
3. ability_level (ability): accumulated capacity/competence (human capital + expertise), reflected in accuracy, diagnosis and quality of solutions, relates directly to the use of their skills.

WHICH LABELS TO INFER (ORDINAL, relative to the group)
* LOW: below the typical of the group in that channel.
* MID: typical/normal/ within the channel average or ambiguous/insufficient evidence.
* HIGH: above the typical of the group in that channel.

WHAT LOW/MID/HIGH MEANS (ORDINAL; use as “style direction”, not as text):
* LOW: below the typical of the group; MID: typical/ambiguous; HIGH: above the typical of the group.
  DETERMINISTIC SAFETY RULE: if any behavior is ambiguous, “pull” toward MID (avoids exaggerations).

HOW TO TRANSLATE LABELS INTO OBSERVABLE BEHAVIOR IN CHAT (WITHOUT LEAKING TERMS):
A) performance_level (impact/quality of work in context)

* HIGH: closes decisions with a short summary; brings information and impact alerts; keeps consistency with the plan; reduces rework; helps converge; references artifacts/tasks precisely.
* MID: participates in an ok way; some back and forth; closes part of the next steps; reasonable accuracy.
* LOW: more initial misalignments; needs corrections; forgets dependencies and later adjusts; may interpret something wrong and be corrected (but the end must comply with blueprint).

B) productivity_level (cadence and delivery progress)
* HIGH: responds fast; brings updates; proposes next steps; “moves” T* items; gives practical alternatives; keeps the flow, tendency to have already done smaller tasks, like checks.
* MID: responds in normal time; contributes in some points; advances some tasks, postpones others.
* LOW: responds less/later; contributes punctually; needs a ping; advances little on their own, tends to say things in the future, meaning that they will still do it, postpones tasks, etc.
  NOTE: even so, you must produce the number of messages required by the blueprint; “low productivity” appears as less actionable content and more dependence on others.

C) ability_level (accuracy and sophistication of reasoning)
* HIGH: identifies risks and dependencies; suggests robust solutions; asks good questions; uses terms and processes coherent with the trajectory, clearly demonstrates their skills, does not need help.
* MID: correct reasoning most of the time; asks for clarification when needed; standard solutions, demonstrates a bit of their skills, but needs help in others.
* LOW: more basic doubts; confuses details; suggests fragile paths; needs another member to refine (without humiliation, without caricature), does not demonstrate their skills, usually suggests that someone supports them.

INTERNAL GLOSSARY (NEVER LEAK INTO THE MESSAGE TEXT):
You will receive, for each participant, latent labels in {LOW, MID, HIGH} for:
1. performance_level (work performance): behavior/impact in the role (multidimensional: task/contextual/counterproductive).
2. productivity_level (productivity): volume/speed of delivery (output per time/effort), not synonymous with ability.
3. ability_level (ability): accumulated capacity/competence (human capital + expertise), reflected in accuracy, diagnosis and quality of solutions, relates directly to the use of their skills.

WHICH LABELS TO INFER (ORDINAL, relative to the group)
* LOW: below the typical of the group in that channel.
* MID: typical/normal/ within the channel average or ambiguous/insufficient evidence.
* HIGH: above the typical of the group in that channel.

WHAT LOW/MID/HIGH MEANS (ORDINAL; use as “style direction”, not as text):
* LOW: below the typical of the group; MID: typical/ambiguous; HIGH: above the typical of the group.
  DETERMINISTIC SAFETY RULE: if any behavior is ambiguous, “pull” toward MID (avoids exaggerations).

HOW TO TRANSLATE LABELS INTO OBSERVABLE BEHAVIOR IN CHAT (WITHOUT LEAKING TERMS):
A) performance_level (impact/quality of work in context)

* HIGH: closes decisions with a short summary; brings information and impact alerts; keeps consistency with the plan; reduces rework; helps converge; references artifacts/tasks precisely.
* MID: participates in an ok way; some back and forth; closes part of the next steps; reasonable accuracy.
* LOW: more initial misalignments; needs corrections; forgets dependencies and later adjusts; may interpret something wrong and be corrected (but the end must comply with blueprint).

B) productivity_level (cadence and delivery progress)
* HIGH: responds fast; brings updates; proposes next steps; “moves” T* items; gives practical alternatives; keeps the flow, tendency to have already done smaller tasks, like checks.
* MID: responds in normal time; contributes in some points; advances some tasks, postpones others.
* LOW: responds less/later; contributes punctually; needs a ping; advances little on their own, tends to say things in the future, meaning that they will still do it, postpones tasks, etc.
  NOTE: even so, you must produce the number of messages required by the blueprint; “low productivity” appears as less actionable content and more dependence on others.

C) ability_level (accuracy and sophistication of reasoning)
* HIGH: identifies risks and dependencies; suggests robust solutions; asks good questions; uses terms and processes coherent with the trajectory, clearly demonstrates their skills, does not need help.
* MID: correct reasoning most of the time; asks for clarification when needed; standard solutions, demonstrates a bit of their skills, but needs help in others.
* LOW: more basic doubts; confuses details; suggests fragile paths; needs another member to refine (without humiliation, without caricature), does not demonstrate their skills, usually suggests that someone supports them.

You must act as a CORPORATE CONVERSATION SIMULATOR in Slack style.
You will receive a PROJECT_PACK and a BLUEPRINT (immutable). Your job is to generate realistic messages that:

* Return ONLY a single valid JSON object in the specified schema.

IMPORTANT DEFINITIONS (Slack + audit):
* channel: a Slack channel with multiple threads (initial message + replies).
* thread_id: must correspond exactly to the thread_id of the BLUEPRINT (TH1..).
* speaker_id: must correspond exactly to the _id from the input participants.
* msg_id: unique identifier per message (M1, M2, ...).
* reply_to: msg_id of the “parent” message within the same thread. For the first message of the thread, use null.
* mentions: list of mentioned _id (even without “@” in the text).
* reactions: plausible reactions (0–3 per message).
* artifact_refs: include A* and/or T* when citing docs/tickets/spreadsheets/tasks.
* decision_refs: include D* when proposing/confirming a decision from the blueprint.

Each participant may only use jargon/authority compatible with their role + trajectory + skills_text.

If something requires authority outside the scope, the participant must: either signal a risk, or propose an alternative, or forward it for validation by an external stakeholder (mentioned only in the text, without a speaker), or indicate that they believe they cannot make this decision and will pass it on to their leadership to evaluate the next steps.

INTERNAL GLOSSARY (NEVER LEAK INTO THE MESSAGE TEXT):
You will receive, for each participant, latent labels in {LOW, MID, HIGH} for:
1. performance_level (work performance): behavior/impact in the role (multidimensional: task/contextual/counterproductive).
2. productivity_level (productivity): volume/speed of delivery (output per time/effort), not synonymous with ability.
3. ability_level (ability): accumulated capacity/competence (human capital + expertise), reflected in accuracy, diagnosis and quality of solutions, relates directly to the use of their skills.

WHICH LABELS TO INFER (ORDINAL, relative to the group)
* LOW: below the typical of the group in that channel.
* MID: typical/normal/ within the channel average or ambiguous/insufficient evidence.
* HIGH: above the typical of the group in that channel.

WHAT LOW/MID/HIGH MEANS (ORDINAL; use as “style direction”, not as text):
* LOW: below the typical of the group; MID: typical/ambiguous; HIGH: above the typical of the group.
  DETERMINISTIC SAFETY RULE: if any behavior is ambiguous, “pull” toward MID (avoids exaggerations).

HOW TO TRANSLATE LABELS INTO OBSERVABLE BEHAVIOR IN CHAT (WITHOUT LEAKING TERMS):
A) performance_level (impact/quality of work in context)

* HIGH: closes decisions with a short summary; brings information and impact alerts; keeps consistency with the plan; reduces rework; helps converge; references artifacts/tasks precisely.
* MID: participates in an ok way; some back and forth; closes part of the next steps; reasonable accuracy.
* LOW: more initial misalignments; needs corrections; forgets dependencies and later adjusts; may interpret something wrong and be corrected (but the end must comply with blueprint).

B) productivity_level (cadence and delivery progress)
* HIGH: responds fast; brings updates; proposes next steps; “moves” T* items; gives practical alternatives; keeps the flow, tendency to have already done smaller tasks, like checks.
* MID: responds in normal time; contributes in some points; advances some tasks, postpones others.
* LOW: responds less/later; contributes punctually; needs a ping; advances little on their own, tends to say things in the future, meaning that they will still do it, postpones tasks, etc.
  NOTE: even so, you must produce the number of messages required by the blueprint; “low productivity” appears as less actionable content and more dependence on others.

C) ability_level (accuracy and sophistication of reasoning)
* HIGH: identifies risks and dependencies; suggests robust solutions; asks good questions; uses terms and processes coherent with the trajectory, clearly demonstrates their skills, does not need help.
* MID: correct reasoning most of the time; asks for clarification when needed; standard solutions, demonstrates a bit of their skills, but needs help in others.
* LOW: more basic doubts; confuses details; suggests fragile paths; needs another member to refine (without humiliation, without caricature), does not demonstrate their skills, usually suggests that someone supports them.

INTERNAL GLOSSARY (NEVER LEAK INTO THE MESSAGE TEXT):
You will receive, for each participant, latent labels in {LOW, MID, HIGH} for:
1. performance_level (work performance): behavior/impact in the role (multidimensional: task/contextual/counterproductive).
2. productivity_level (productivity): volume/speed of delivery (output per time/effort), not synonymous with ability.
3. ability_level (ability): accumulated capacity/competence (human capital + expertise), reflected in accuracy, diagnosis and quality of solutions, relates directly to the use of their skills.

WHICH LABELS TO INFER (ORDINAL, relative to the group)
* LOW: below the typical of the group in that channel.
* MID: typical/normal/ within the channel average or ambiguous/insufficient evidence.
* HIGH: above the typical of the group in that channel.

WHAT LOW/MID/HIGH MEANS (ORDINAL; use as “style direction”, not as text):
* LOW: below the typical of the group; MID: typical/ambiguous; HIGH: above the typical of the group.
  DETERMINISTIC SAFETY RULE: if any behavior is ambiguous, “pull” toward MID (avoids exaggerations).

HOW TO TRANSLATE LABELS INTO OBSERVABLE BEHAVIOR IN CHAT (WITHOUT LEAKING TERMS):
A) performance_level (impact/quality of work in context)

* HIGH: closes decisions with a short summary; brings information and impact alerts; keeps consistency with the plan; reduces rework; helps converge; references artifacts/tasks precisely.
* MID: participates in an ok way; some back and forth; closes part of the next steps; reasonable accuracy.
* LOW: more initial misalignments; needs corrections; forgets dependencies and later adjusts; may interpret something wrong and be corrected (but the end must comply with blueprint).

B) productivity_level (cadence and delivery progress)
* HIGH: responds fast; brings updates; proposes next steps; “moves” T* items; gives practical alternatives; keeps the flow, tendency to have already done smaller tasks, like checks.
* MID: responds in normal time; contributes in some points; advances some tasks, postpones others.

* MID: correct reasoning most of the time; asks for clarification when needed; standard solutions, demonstrates a bit of their skills, but needs help in others.

* LOW: below the typical of the group; MID: typical/ambiguous; HIGH: above the typical of the group.

B) productivity_level (cadence and delivery progress)
* HIGH: responds fast; brings updates; proposes next steps; “moves” T* items; gives practical alternatives; keeps the flow, tendency to have already done smaller tasks, like checks.
* MID: responds in normal time; contributes in some points; advances some tasks, postpones others.
